key_insights: Aerospace is no longer a macro-agnostic buy-the-dip group. The market has become more stock-specific than thematic. Stocks are trading like March/April (higher jet fuel, fears of a global travel slowdown), but the Middle East conflict is now 7-8 months old and jet fuel is still elevated.
Maintenance decisions had no time to adjust in March. Time is now working against the growth outlook because the fuel pressure has persisted.
Investors wanted to add length in aerospace on the original equipment side, including BA and its supply chain. Multiple issues have tempered that enthusiasm.

Aerospace positioning per the desk: more owned are BA, RBC, CRS, ATI and DPC, with investors warming to HONA on valuation. More debated are WWD (needs to guide) and HWM (debate over the CPP deal). Underowned are TDG, HEI and TXT.

Defense primes have acted poorly even during risk-off and geopolitical escalation. The desk hosted a dinner with GS's global head of aerospace and defense investment banking that surfaced potential sources of weakness, and it offers details on request.

The potential midterm blue wave is a clear overhang on defense. The desk also believes SPCX lock-ups add pressure. Investors are more positive on LMT and GD, mixed on RTX, and more negative on NOC and LHX. Fed IT remains a source of funds, with debate over whether DOGE could reaccelerate.
SU FP is down 10% pre-market on a $24bn acquisition of PTC.
Equipment rental names show positive Q3 checks on better time utilization, extending lead times and rates that improved quarter over quarter.
BA saw incrementally positive headlines on the software glitch, which is not being viewed as a safety issue.

GS Eco expects Q3 2026 earnings season to start the week of October 12, with about 70% of S&P 500 market cap reported by end of October. Consensus expects S&P 500 y/y EPS growth of 27% in Q3 versus 33% realized in Q2, excluding accounting distortions.

GS Eco says AI infrastructure beneficiaries account for over 50% of S&P 500 EPS growth this quarter, with hyperscaler capex growth of 116%. Median S&P 500 stock EPS growth is expected to slow from 14% in Q2 to 9% in Q3.

GS Eco expects most companies to beat consensus again. Input cost pressure will likely limit sequential margin expansion and the dollar is a smaller tailwind to revenue growth. Recent economic growth data are strong and earnings revision breadth remains positive.

DAL reports Friday October 9 pre-market at 6:30am, call at 10am, with a 6% implied move. Moves have been muted over the last four quarters. The desk expects a full-year guidance update with an implied Q4. Airline revenue trends are strong to better, but costs are worse both including and excluding fuel.

DAL is more protected than peers on balance, with better margins and ownership of Trainer. That has taken the stock to relative highs and set an elevated bar. Full-year guidance is EPS $6.50-7.50 and FCF $3-4bn. The Street is at $5.89 EPS, below the low end, with Q4 topline growth expected at +17% y/y.

RPM reports Tuesday pre-market around 6:45am, call at 10am, with a 4% implied move. It is fiscal Q1, so fewer updates to full-year guidance are likely. The stock has been consistently green when reporting fiscal Q1 in recent years.

RPM valuation suggests very low sentiment. Consensus fiscal 2027 EBITDA growth sits at the midpoint of the +5-10% guide. Q1 looks easy sequentially. The desk is looking for topline color across CPG, PCG and Consumer, with cost headwinds potentially building.

Morning market color: Bolsonaro took a surprise lead in Brazil's first-round presidential vote. Spain's PM called a snap election for late November, helping send the euro to 17-month lows. French stocks are off 105bps. WTI is $91, Brent $102, the 10-year is 5.28%, DXY is $102 and Bitcoin is $86k. ISM Services is due later today.
